title: 2026 Q2 QBR - Terra Analytics Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review covering usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer is leaning toward a hybrid approach (hosted + dedicated reserve) but has questions on encryption/KMS, SOC 2 artifacts, and predictable pricing for Q3 pilot. Action: Redwood to share detailed usage/cost breakdown, SOC 2 pack, and schedule a technical deep-dive for private deployment feasibility.
action_items: Omar Ruiz: Share Q1-Q2 token usage breakdown and projected cost vs forecast (due: 2026-05-20)
Lucas Park: Schedule technical deep-dive and benchmark slot for private deployment (due: 2026-05-22)
Maya Chen: Send pricing spreadsheet for Dedicated pools + pilot terms (due: 2026-05-18)
Priya Rao: Provide list of compliance docs they need for procurement (due: 2026-05-19)
next_steps: Redwood to send usage and cost workbook
Schedule SE technical deep-dive to scope private deployment and network requirements
Agree on pilot scope (3-week Dedicated pilot, X GPUs) and success criteria
Customer to share procurement timeline and required security artifacts
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Maya from Redwood here, with Omar and Lucas. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Liam: Good thanks, Liam here. Appreciate you carving out the time for the QBR.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, Priya on my side. We have about 50 mins.
[00:15] Maya: Great, we'll keep it tight. Quick agenda \u0014 usage trends, cost, any reliability items, and then roadmap and next steps. Sound good?
[00:22] Noah: Sounds good.
[00:24] [00:30] Omar: I'll kick off with usage. We've seen Terra's token volume up ~3x since Jan, driven by summary workloads and embeddings for search. The burst windows are around 9\u001311am and then late batch jobs at night.
[00:45] Liam: Yeah that's right. The embeddings spike is from the nightly ingest job, and the summary calls are from the new customer support flow.
[00:52] Lucas: Quick question \u0014 are you using prefix caching for the summaries or are those mostly cold starts?
[00:57] Priya: Mostly cold, we tried the built-in cache but it's tricky because the prompts change a lot.
[01:05] Lucas: Got it. If you're open, we can suggest a hybrid approach \u0014 keeping frequently asked templates in KV cache and batching the rest. Might cut token cost without hurting latency.
[01:18] Priya: That would help. We're seeing cost blowouts at end of month.
[01:21] [01:30] Maya: On cost, we pulled a high-level view \u0014 you're currently on hosted and a small dedicated pool for nightly batch, the latter hasn't been fully utilized. Your unit cost for generation is about 35% higher than projected because of small batch sizes and cold KV cache.
[01:47] Liam: Hm. Is that mostly because of quantization profiles or batching?
[01:51] Omar: It's a combination. Also some of the models in the catalog are higher compute. We flagged a few routes where a smaller quantized model provides near-identical quality at 40% lower token cost.
[02:06] Liam: Can you send that list?
[02:08] Maya: Absolutely, we'll include a recommended model + quantization mapping in the workbook.
[02:13] [02:20] Priya: Another thing \u0014 we've got procurement asking about dedicated nodes for data residency. They want SLA and audit logs. Are those packaged in Redwood Dedicated?
[02:30] Maya: Yes Dedicated includes dedicated GPU pools, per-route SLAs, and audit logs. For Private (VPC) we can also do customer-managed control plane and KMS integration.
[02:40] Noah: For KMS \u0014 is HSM support available or only KMS?
[02:44] Lucas: We support KMS integrations today, and HSM via our Private/on-prem options; it's a slightly different onboarding path, but doable.
[02:52] [03:00] Priya: How about SOC 2 and other compliance artifacts \u0014 procurement wants evidence.
[03:05] Omar: We have a SOC 2 Type II report and a compliance pack \u0014 we'll share the pack link after the call.
[03:12] Priya: Perfect.
[03:15] [03:30] Liam: We did have two incidents in March and April where latency spiked in hosted during the ingest window. Can you explain root cause?
[03:40] Lucas: Yeah, I pulled the traces \u0014 March was a batch scheduling collision causing queueing; April was a model fallback sequence that increased load on the smaller pool. We applied routing policy changes and it stabilized.
[03:54] Liam: Ok, can you add the incident timeline to the workbook?
[03:57] Maya: Yes we'll include incident summaries and the mitigations we applied.
[04:02] [04:30] Priya: On the dedicated pool \u0014 we want to test a dedicated pilot for Q3. What's a realistic pilot size?
[04:38] Lucas: For your workload pattern I'd recommend a 4-GPU reserved pool for three weeks to validate throughput and cost. We can run benchmarks with your busiest routes.
[04:48] Liam: And pricing during pilot?
[04:51] Maya: We typically offer pilot pricing with a reduced monthly commitment and a consumption-based top-up. I'll send the pricing spreadsheet.
[05:00] [05:30] Noah: Network-wise \u0014 if we do Private, we'll need to ensure the VPC peering and firewall rules are aligned. Any special port requirements?
[05:40] Lucas: Standard egress to Redwood control plane plus gRPC endpoints; we'll send a network checklist. In some transcriptions it was listed as \"g r p c\" but that's gRPC.
[05:51] Priya: Good. Also curious about model rollouts \u0014 can we pin model versions during the pilot?
[05:58] Omar: Yes pinning and canary rollouts are supported in Console, you can define rollout percentages and automatic rollback.
[06:05] [06:30] Liam: On data retention \u0014 we need logs to be purged after 90 days for some projects. Can we set retention per route?
[06:38] Lucas: We support configurable retention at the route level for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has default retention but we can discuss enterprise options.
[06:47] Priya: That's important for us.
[06:50] [07:10] Maya: Let's talk success criteria \u0014 what would make the pilot a win for Terra?
[07:14] Liam: Throughput needs to hit at least 95% of our peak SLA during 9\u001311am windows, and cost per generated token should be no more than 15% above our internal target.
[07:25] Priya: And minimal operational overhead \u0014 we don't want to be running patches or manual configs daily.
[07:31] Maya: Good notes. We'll outline measurable SLOs in the pilot doc.
[07:36] [08:00] Lucas: One technical note \u0014 if you adopt KV cache more aggressively for support prompts we can reduce median latency by ~30ms and cut duplicate token usage.
[08:12] Priya: That 30ms is big for the UI. We'll take that.
[08:16] [08:30] Liam: Anything on embeddings cost? They said embedding calls are dominating compute.
[08:38] Omar: We're seeing many 1:1 embedding calls; batching and async dedupe can reduce calls by 45%. We'll propose a batching window.
[08:48] Priya: We can change the ingest to do larger batches every hour rather than per-file.
[08:52] [09:00] Maya: Quick interjection \u0014 procurement asked about SSO and RBAC. We support SAML/SSO and role-based access; we can map to your groups.
[09:10] Noah: Great \u0014 do you support SCIM provisioning?
[09:14] Lucas: Yes SCIM is available.
[09:17] [09:30] Priya: Any concerns about vendor lock? Some stakeholders asked if we'd be able to move workloads off Redwood easily.
[09:38] Maya: We provide model/route export and data export features; the goal is to make vendor transitions possible though there are always work involved in adapting prompts and infra.
[09:48] Liam: Fair.
[09:50] [10:00] Noah: I want to make sure the pricing model for Dedicated vs Hosted is explicit \u0014 do you have unit cost examples?
[10:08] Maya: We'll include unit cost per 1M tokens with and without quantization profiling in the workbook.
[10:15] [10:30] Lucas: Also we'll include a set of recommended kernel/quantization settings per route, that was mis-transcribed sometimes as \"kernal\" but it's kernel.
[10:40] Priya: Ha, noted.
[10:44] [11:00] Liam: Any blockers on our side for the pilot?
[11:04] Priya: We'll need the SOC 2 pack, network checklist and a draft contract to start procurement.
[11:10] Maya: We'll send those after the call.
[11:13] [11:30] Omar: One more ops note \u0014 we'll propose a cadence for check-ins during the pilot: weekly health sync + on-call for incidents.
[11:40] Liam: Weekly makes sense.
[11:43] [12:00] Priya: On SLAs \u0014 is there a credit policy if we miss uptime?
[12:06] Maya: Yes Dedicated has SLA credits; we'll include the terms in the contract template.
[12:12] [12:30] Lucas: For benchmarks, could you share a small representative prompt set? We'll run with your data patterns to get realistic numbers.
[12:39] Priya: We can share a sanitized subset.
[12:44] [13:00] Noah: Anything else from Redwood?
[13:03] Maya: No, just to confirm next steps.
[13:07] Omar: We'll send the usage workbook, SOC 2 pack, pricing, and schedule the SE deep-dive.
[13:15] Liam: Great. Thanks everyone.
[13:18] Priya: Thanks.
[13:20] [13:30] Maya: Recap \u0014 action items we'll follow up on; Lucas will reach out to schedule benchmarks. Meeting adjourned.
[13:35] [End 52:00]
